reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: There is evidence of target engagement - anti-drug antibody formation was observed for PDR001, LAG525, and ACZ885, indicating the drugs reached their targets and elicited immune responses. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Downstream biology did change as predicted - increases in tumor infiltrating T cells, TIL activation, and T-cell inflamed signature were observed, indicating immune pathway activation. A favorable biomarker profile was seen in 4.8-16.7% of participants. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite biological activity, clinical endpoints failed dramatically. ORR ranged from only 4.7% to 14.3% across all arms, well below what would be expected for effective melanoma treatment. PFS was uniformly poor at 2.7-2.8 months across arms. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported that might identify responder populations. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial had adequate duration (213 weeks) and reasonable sample size (196 patients). However, significant safety concerns emerged with multiple serious cardiac and autoimmune adverse events including myocarditis, acute MI, and autoimmune colitis, with on-treatment deaths across all arms. This represents a classic 'biology moved but endpoint flat' scenario where target engagement and pathway modulation occurred but failed to translate to meaningful clinical benefit.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear evidence of target engagement (anti-drug antibodies) and pathway modulation (increased TILs, T-cell activation, favorable biomarker profiles in subset), but ORR remained very low (4.7-14.3%) across all combination arms despite biological activity
